migration_guide: Step 1: Add springdoc-openapi-starter-webmvc-ui dependency (version 2.3.0) to pom.xml for all three services
Step 2: Configure Swagger in application.yml - set springdoc.api-docs.path=/api-docs and springdoc.swagger-ui.path=/swagger-ui.html
Step 3: Create SwaggerConfiguration class in infrastructure/config package for each service with OpenAPI bean definition
Step 4: Add @Tag annotation to all controller classes for logical grouping in Swagger UI
Step 5: Add @Operation annotations to all controller methods with summary and description
Step 6: Add @ApiResponses with @ApiResponse for all possible HTTP status codes (200, 201, 400, 401, 403, 404, 500, 503)
Step 7: Add @Parameter annotations to all method parameters with descriptions and examples
Step 8: Add @SecurityRequirement(name='bearerAuth') to all authenticated endpoints
Step 9: Define security schemes in SwaggerConfiguration (JWT Bearer authentication)
Step 10: Add @Schema annotations to all DTO classes and fields with descriptions and examples
Step 11: Run mvn clean install to download dependencies and compile code
Step 12: Start each service using mvn spring-boot:run
Step 13: Access Swagger UI at http://localhost:{port}/swagger-ui.html for each service
Step 14: Test JWT authentication by logging in via User Management Service and using 'Authorize' button in Swagger UI
Step 15: Download OpenAPI specifications from http://localhost:{port}/api-docs for documentation and client generation
Step 16: For production, disable Swagger UI by setting springdoc.swagger-ui.enabled=false in application-prod.yml
Step 17: Configure CORS if Swagger UI will be accessed from different domains
Step 18: Set up API Gateway to route Swagger UI requests to appropriate microservices
Step 19: Generate client SDKs using OpenAPI Generator with downloaded specifications
Step 20: Integrate Swagger specifications into CI/CD pipeline for automated API documentation updates
